issues.legal_issue: After an agency is revoked, an agent who occupies premises on the principal’s behalf under an agreement authorizing the principal to resume occupation cannot remain there or interfere with the principal’s business, and the principal may obtain a temporary injunction.
material_facts: The principal was the tenant of the premises and had placed the agent there to conduct the principal’s business.
The agreement permitted the principal to occupy the premises after removing the agent and did not grant the agent a right to remain after termination.
The principal terminated the agency, and the agent prevented the principal and its replacement agent from conducting business at the premises.
issues.conclusion: The agent had no right to remain in the premises or interfere with the principal’s business; the temporary injunction should be restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 202, 205 and 221 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, revocation ordinarily terminates an agent’s actual authority unless the agency is coupled with an interest; an agent may be entitled to compensation or a lien in appropriate circumstances, but a lien is subject to an inconsistent agreement and cannot be used to obstruct the principal’s business. The Court also relied on the principle that an agent obtains no interest in property held for the principal, as discussed in Foley v. Hill and Smt. Chandrakantaben v. Vadilal Bapalal Modi. It noted that not every agency is fiduciary, and that the nature of the relationship depends on the authority and confidence involved.

rule.if: appeal_from_vacated_temporary_injunction and agency_terminated and agent_possession_for_principal and agreement_allows_principal_to_resume_premises

predicates.appeal_from_vacated_temporary_injunction: The principal appealed after a court vacated a temporary injunction protecting its business or occupation of premises.
predicates.agency_terminated: The principal ended the agent’s authority to act for it.
predicates.agent_possession_for_principal: The agent occupied the premises on behalf of the principal to conduct the principal’s business.
predicates.agreement_allows_principal_to_resume_pre: The agency agreement allowed the principal to occupy the premises after removing the agent.
predicates.temporary_injunction_restored: The principal receives a temporary injunction preventing the agent from interfering with its business or occupation of the premises.

issues.definition: When the principal appeals the vacating of a temporary injunction, has ended the agency, and the agent occupied the premises for the principal under an agreement allowing the principal to resume occupation, the injunction is restored.

issues.legal_issue: A principal need not first bring a suit to recover possession where the agent’s occupation of the principal’s premises was only on the principal’s behalf and not in the agent’s own right.
material_facts: The principal held the lease to the premises and had allowed the agent to occupy them only to conduct the principal’s business.
The agent did not hold the premises in an independent capacity, and the principal’s possession was treated as continuing through the agent.
The agent’s agency was terminated, after which the agent obstructed the principal’s business at the premises.
issues.conclusion: Because the agent’s possession was on the principal’s behalf, the principal did not need to sue for recovery of possession before obtaining an injunction.
issues.legal_principle: An agent who holds property for a principal obtains no interest in it, cannot deny the principal’s title, and holds possession as the principal’s possession. The Court relied on Foley v. Hill, Smt. Chandrakantaben v. Vadilal Bapalal Modi, David Lyell v. John Lawson Kennedy, Williams v. Pott, and Narayani Amma v. Bhaskaran Pillai. It held that the general rule requiring a plaintiff out of possession to seek recovery of possession does not apply in the same way to a dispute between principal and agent over property held for the principal; it distinguished Abdul Nabi Sahib v. Bajab Sahib and Jemma v. Raghu.

predicates.principal_agent_property_dispute: The dispute concerns a principal seeking to protect its rights against an agent in relation to the principal’s property.
predicates.agent_possession_for_principal: The agent occupied or held the property on behalf of the principal.
predicates.agent_has_no_independent_possession_righ: The agent had no right to possess the property independently of the agency.
predicates.recovery_suit_unnecessary_before_injunct: The principal need not first obtain a separate order recovering possession before seeking an injunction.

issues.definition: When a principal-agent property dispute involves an agent who possesses property only for the principal and has no independent right to possess it, a separate recovery suit is not a prerequisite to an injunction.
